newsitem.title: UK: Caribbean 1996 sugar output highest for decade - SAC.
newsitem.headline: Caribbean 1996 sugar output highest for decade - SAC.

text.p: Sugar production in Caribbean sugar economies reached 826,660 tonnes in 1996, highest in the last 10 years and 67,160 tonnes up on 1995, the Sugar Association of the Caribbean (SAC) said on Thursday.
The result was in line with a SAC forecast issued in May.
The SAC, a grouping within the Africa, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) sugar growers' body, said 1997 output was provisionally forecast at 871,407 tonnes.
"It is apparent that the decline of sugar production in the late 1980s has been reversed," the SAC said in a statement.

Sugar exports to the European Union totalled 558,914 tonnes in 1996 compared with 422,328 tonnes in 1995. These exports provided the region with around $404 million in foreign exchange earnings in 1996 after a previous $300 million, the SAC said.
SAC countries had an initial allocation under the USDA's Sugar Import Tariff Rate Quota of 85,146 tonnes, with a potential quota of up to 114,117 tonnes, it said.
The SAC's directors proposed to lobby the US administration for SAC shortfalls to be reallocated among other SAC quota holders so that the region would not lose revenue.
In 1996, the SAC received a US quota allocation of 110,977 tonnes, compared with 72,651 tonnes in 1995.
The directors of the SAC held their 119th meeting in St Kitts on November 7 and 8, the statement said.
